notes: Weights operate on min-max normalized metrics (0-1) across all scored candidates. Three metrics exist: intelligenceIndex (Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index), speed (performance.median_output_tokens_per_second, falling back to performance_v3.mean_output_tokens_per_second) and costEfficiency (1 / estimated cost per task). Cost per task = AA's measured cost to run one Intelligence Index task x (provider blended price / AA blended price), both blended at the category's outputToInputRatio (default 3 output tokens per input token). This prices in how many tokens a model actually spends, not just its per-token price. Per-token pricing is a documented simplification since Copilot (plan + credits) and OpenCode Go (flat monthly plan with per-model caps) aren't priced per token. A model is scored only if it has all of intelligence, speed, cost per task and AA pricing; nothing is estimated or zero-filled. Since Intelligence Index v5 (2026-10-28) Artificial Analysis no longer publishes a Coding or Agentic Index, and its v5 Capability Indexes correlate with intelligence at r>0.99, so intelligence is the only quality signal. expectedIntelligenceIndexVersion pins the index version these weights were chosen for; the pipeline fails when AA reports a different one, so a human re-checks the API before rankings change. topNPerProvider is the shortlist size within each individual provider -- there is no cross-provider ranking, since the choice is which provider's own lineup to use, not a mixed list.

agenticCoding.description: Left running for hours in a loop to solve a problem autonomously with minimal supervision (e.g. an OpenSpec/plan executor, a long-running coding agent).

codeReview.description: Reviewing code written by a different model, reasoning about correctness/design in context rather than driving tools itself.

softwareFactory.description: Executing well-scoped, already-planned coding tasks (e.g. from an OpenSpec change or a larger model's plan) -- throughput and cost matter more than raw intelligence.

llmWiki.description: Maintaining an LLM-curated markdown knowledge base (Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern): ingesting sources into many cross-linked pages, answering from the wiki with citations, and periodically linting it for contradictions, stale claims and orphan pages. Read-heavy and run repeatedly; faithfulness and synthesis matter more than coding skill.
llmWiki.notes: outputToInputRatio 0.2 (1 output token per 5 input tokens): each operation reads a source plus many existing pages and writes comparatively small edits. intelligenceIndex stands in for the signals that matter most here -- long-context reasoning, hallucination rate and instruction following -- which the free Artificial Analysis endpoint does not expose as separate scores. Context window size is not scored because no data source provides it.
